messages:
Marta: sketching a new hybrid loadgen to validate kernel selector heuristics + KV effects. goal: apples-to-apples latency + kernel handoff accounting. dropping the config and quick plan here.

Daniel: nice, paste the generator shape. are you doing both replay + synthetic?

Marta: yes. baseline deterministic replay of 2k traces, then synthetic hybrid: kv-warmup, staircase ramp, steady, clustered microbursts, and a heavy-tail sprinkle. sample phase list (readable form):
seed: 3123; phases: [kv_warmup coverage=0.7 dur=60s, staircase steps=50->200 dur=120s, steady qps=300 dur=300s, clusters peak=4500 burst_ms=1200 clusters=10 inter_s=18, heavy_tail base=30 multiplier=15 dur=200s]

Sam: Metrics to capture for apples-to-apples?

Marta: p50/p90/p95/p99, kernel_switch_events (timestamped), batch_util_time_series, avg_batch_size, kv_lookup_latency_dist, kv_hit_rate_ts, tokens_per_gpu_sec, and a simple cost proxy. also keep perf counters and flamegraphs for handoff windows.

Alex: add a deterministic replay baseline (the 2k traces) so we can directly attribute diffs to selector logic. also plan a seed sweep of 8 seeds for CI.

infra-bot: bench job queued: bench/hybrid-smoke:seed=3123 at 2799999000 :gear:

Daniel: first pass results in. summary: STATIC pin (kernel A): p95 240ms p99 910ms; ADAPT aggressive (kernel B): p95 190ms p99 680ms but kernel_handoffs spiked during clusters (avg 3.8/min); avg_batch_size STATIC=13 ADAPT=40; kv_hit_rate plateau STATIC=0.72 ADAPT drop to 0.56 during clusters; tokens_gpu_s ADAPT +29%

Marta: saw 10-15ms per handoff where cache metadata serialize/unbind runs. flame snapshot top stacks: decoder_attention, batch_coalescer, kv_cache_lookup, cache_eviction_worker, rpc_dispatch.

Alex: hypothesis: aggressive batching defers KV writes or reorders write visibility, raising misses on sudden clustered requests that need recently-created prefixes.

Marta: tried kv_sensitive selector tweak: base_cap=12 max_cap=128 growth_policy=kv_sensitive kv_hit_thresh=0.7 growth_low=+3 growth_high=+10 kv_write_lat_thresh_ms=6 handoff_penalty_ms=10

Marta: kv_sensitive run quick stats: p95 202ms p99 510ms kernel_handoffs/min 1.1 kv_hit_rate_during_clusters 0.69 tokens_gpu_s down ~4% vs ADAPT.

Sam: decent tail win. suggest next: push clusters to 6k, enable optional prefetch of predicted prefixes, measure cold-miss recovery time (time until kv_hit_rate for affected prefix returns >0.6).

Daniel: also write a histogram-compare utility: take deterministic baseline traces, resample to match QPS curves, then run KS-test and report quantile deltas normalized by batch-size to keep apples-to-apples.

Marta: added tests: deterministic baseline, hybrid synth at 2k/4k/6k peaks, seed sweep 8 seeds, artifact retention. artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/hybrid-smoke/2799999000/seed-3123/

Alex: one more metric: measure per-prefix cold-miss recovery latency distribution and the time-weighted KV hit-rate penalty during the 30s after cluster start. that will quantify user-visible regressions.

Marta: will record those. initial conclusion: aggressive batching boosts throughput and mid-tail latencies but can amplify KV cold-miss exposure during short intense clusters. KV-aware growth caps and modest prefetching reduce p99 and kernel handoffs at a small throughput cost. will enqueue CI runs and draft a short RFC if results are consistent across seeds.

Sam: :thumbsup:

Marta: ping me for artifacts or to tweak cluster cadence. thanks!
